records.text: I think Charlie Kirk's second redundant microphone was rigged as a shaped charge intended to hit his chest but accidentally hit his neck.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I think his mic, the second redundant mic was rigged and it was meant to hit his chest. ... And then I think they had to pivot, because the shaped charge accidentally—instead of hitting his chest and causing that .30-06 diameter, as would happen with PETN explosives, as we've demonstrated to you in the past—it accidentally, because of how Charlie (Charlie Kirk) was crouched... ... It went up and hit his neck.

verification.notes: This is explicitly framed as a theory. Current charging records and 2026 hearing testimony allege a rooftop rifle shot and contain physical and video evidence supporting that allegation, while no forensic source supports a microphone shaped charge. Because the criminal case is pending and the available bullet analysis has limits, the unsupported theory is recorded as unverifiable rather than false.

records.text: My theory is that Terrell Farnsworth scrambled to remove the camera's SD card because the alleged shaped-charge plan did not go as expected.

appearances.snippet: It's the reason why Terrell (Terrell Farnsworth) had to scramble to get the cameras down, because they were never supposed to see it. ... Again, this is my theory, and I am now very much sticking to it. Okay, they panicked.

verification.notes: Later public footage and testimony support that Terrell Farnsworth handled recording media after the shooting, but no source establishes that he did so because a shaped-charge plan failed. The claimed motive and conspiracy remain speculation without named or forensic evidence.

records.text: Shaped charges are common in improvised explosive devices, copper is their most common material, and even a wine bottle can be used to make one.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #5 (Ep VMNWMXX1vO8)

appearances.snippet: As far as the shaped charge, it is very common in IEDs, and copper is the most common. ... But to give you a sense of how easy it is, you can use a wine bottle to make one as well.

verification.notes: Authoritative mine-action references document shaped-charge IEDs made with copper jet-forming liners and an improvised shaped charge made from a wine bottle and plastic explosive. NIST also defines the metal-lined directional effect. The compound technical claim is supported.

records.text: My technical friends and I believe Charlie Kirk was hit by the microphone rather than a gun, although we could be biased because we work with improvised explosive devices.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #5 (Ep VMNWMXX1vO8)

appearances.snippet: I know this won't help progress your theories, but me, along with my tech friends, all believe it was the mic. ... We could definitely be biased since we deal with IEDs, but I just thought that you should know that a lot of people who deal with rifles and improvised explosives do not believe it was from a gun.

verification.notes: The episode reads an anonymous message asserting this belief, but the sender and claimed technical credentials cannot be authenticated. Current official evidence alleges a firearm shot, and no forensic source supports a microphone device, so the private opinion has no verifiable evidentiary basis.

records.text: An anonymous anesthesiologist said a shaped charge in Charlie Kirk's RØDE microphone was the best fit for the visible evidence and the coroner's reported findings.
records.speaker: Anonymous anesthesiologist email source (Ep iB-YtO3UZOg)

appearances.snippet: That is not what we saw. A shaped charge in the RØDE microphone would have sent a projectile from his right anterior chest upward and leftward, likely exiting from his left neck or entering his cervical spine. ... The projectile would have almost certainly damaged both lungs and possibly his heart. In other words, there would have been pulmonary hemorrhaging and possibly hemorrhaging around the heart as well. ... The exploding mic is thus the best fit from what we could see in what the coroner reported.

verification.notes: This is an anonymous medical opinion based on limited video and a reportedly described coroner finding. The writer's identity and credentials are not authenticated, the referenced complete medical-examiner materials are not supplied, and current official case records attribute the death to a firearm. The shaped-charge theory cannot be established from the available evidence.

records.text: An anonymous anesthesiologist opined that Charlie Kirk was killed by a shaped charge on his right chest and accused his security team of removing him in a highly rehearsed fashion before others could see what happened.
records.speaker: Anonymous anesthesiologist email source (Ep iB-YtO3UZOg)

appearances.snippet: In my estimation, he was murdered from a shaped charge on his right chest, and his security team did their best in a highly rehearsed fashion to get him the hell out of there before anybody could see what happened.

verification.notes: The accusation comes from an unauthenticated anonymous email, and Owens immediately identified it as somebody else's opinion. No physical or official evidence located supports a shaped charge or a rehearsed security-team removal to conceal it. Official filings instead allege a rifle shooting, but the anonymous accusation itself cannot be conclusively adjudicated from the public record.

records.text: Owens said she believed the evidence showed Charlie Kirk was hit by a shaped charge and that there was no gun on the rooftop.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: We'll stop there. But yeah, you get the point. And I do believe that there is so much evidence there that that's what happened, that he got hit by a shaped charge. And I think that there was no gun on the rooftop.

verification.notes: The primary transcript confirms Owens said she believed a shaped charge caused Kirk's injury and that no gun was on the roof. Her belief attribution is accurate. The underlying theory conflicts with current official and hearing evidence describing a rooftop shooter, a recovered rifle, firearm-related cartridge evidence, and DNA links; because Robinson remains accused and the case is not a conviction, the note preserves that procedural status.
